Thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of L.D. 720. Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston ("FHLBank Boston") is one of eleven regional Federal Home Loan Banks (FHLBanks) chartered by Congress in 1932. Banks, credit unions, insurance companies, and community development financial institutions located in the six New
England states are eligible to join FHLBank Boston as a member. FHLBank Boston currently has four (4) Mainedomiciled insurance companies.`

BACKGROUND:

The FHLBanks, which were formed by Congress in 1932 in response to the Great Depression, are cooperatively structured, member-owned wholesale banks that provide highly reliable wholesale funding to our members to support housing finance and community development. The FHLBanks are regulated by the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA). In order to access FHLBank funding, members pledge collateral, primarily consisting of residential loans or securities backed by residential loans. Members can thus "liquefy" their residential mortgage assets by pledging them to support their FHLBank borrowings, using the proceeds from those borrowings for further lending and investment within their communities. In this way, the FHLBanks support housing finance and the local economy.

In 2024, in partnership with our members, FHLBank Boston also contributed more than $35 million to our Affordable Housing Program and an additional $24.9 million for programs that help lower- and moderate-income
homebuyers and support job creation and community development throughout New England. Specific to Maine, FHLBank Boston's affordable housing and community development programs had the following impact in 2024:

The FHLBanks' government sponsored enterprise status enables us to borrow funds in global capital markets at attractive rates and pass on the benefit of such low-cost funds to our members by making loans to them on very narrow margins. Having access to this reliable source of liquidity helps our insurance company members manage their balance sheets more efficiently and build capital to protect policyholders. Unlike commercial lenders that may halt lending to insurance companies at times when they face their own liquidity pressures, FHLBanks have historically been able to maintain access to the global capital markets and continue lending to our members across business cycles, including during times of economic and market stress. The events in the banking industry in March 2023 further highlighted the importance of the FHLBanks. When the banking industry became destabilized as a result of a few highprofile bank failures, the FHLBanks stepped up to meet the needs of our depository institution members by raising record amounts of funding in the global capital markets.
While the 2023 bank failures were largely a non-event for the insurance industry, the amendments to the Maine insurance receivership laws contained in L.D. 720 are designed to enable the FHLBanks to sen/e our Maine insurance company members when market forces or more unique circumstances create a liquidity need, just as we are able to do for our Maine depository institution members. Consequently, with the amendments to the Maine insurance receivership laws contained in L.D. 720, FHLBanks can help protect the Maine consumers, who are the policyholders of a struggling insurance company member, from the uncertainty and confusion that can result from the sudden, chaotic collapse of an insurance company.
PRESENT LAW:
As a government sponsored enterprise, FHLBank Boston is heavily regulated by the FHFA and is only permitted to advance funds to its members on a fully secured basis. Due to disparities between federal banking law and state insurance law, and concern over those disparities on the pan of our regulator, FHLBank Boston's credit posture must be more conservative toward our Maine-domiciled insurance company members than our Maine bank

2

and credit union members?
A central reason for this disparity is that Maine insurance law does not provide the same protections that are
afforded to the FHLBanks under federal banking law. For example, Maine insurance law gives the receiver broad powers to settle an insolvent insurance company's affairs, which could result in FHLBank Boston, as secured creditor, being subjected to a lengthy stay or injunction delaying its statutory right to resort to its collateral or subjected to a "voidable transfer' or similar challenge to its secured position. Due to protections specific to the FHLBanks that are built into federal banking law, FHLBank Boston does not face these risks when it lends to bank and credit union members in Maine. importantly, under existing Maine insurance law, a secured creditor is entitled to the value of its collateral in an insolvency proceeding. Moreover, existing Maine commercial law, namely, the Uniform Commercial Code as implemented in the state, governs the priority of FHLBank Boston's security interest in its collateral. Therefore, L.D. 720 does not improve the priority of FHLBank Boston's security interest in its collateral nor does L.D. 720 provide FHLBank with additional collateral. Instead, such amendments merely allow the FHLBank Boston to liquidate its collateral on a timely basis if necessary.
ARGUMENT IN FAVOR:
By equalizing the noted disparities between state and federal law, L.D. 720 will enable FHLBank Boston to equalize its approach to lending to insurance company members, on the one hand, and bank and credit union members, on the other hand, in Maine. Moreover, while there have only been three instances of a FHLBank insurance company member going into a receivership in the 93-year history of the FHLBank system, L.D. 720 addresses concerns raised by the FHLBanks` federal regulator, the FHFA.
L.D. 720 includes terms recommended by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners that subject the FHLBank to a short stay period in the event of an insurance company receivership (10 days) and require the FHLBank to work closely with the Maine Bureau of Insurance (or their appointed receiver) during that short stay period to, among other things, develop a timeline for the release of excess collateral and the redemption or repurchase of FHLBank stock. L.D. 720 also mirrors a model act adopted by the National Council of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL) during their annual meeting in July 2023.
The certainty provided to the FHLBank (and the Maine Bureau of Insurance) through L.D. 720 will enable the FHLBank to continue to lend to a Maine insurance company member when it needs funding the most and additional liquidity may be the only thing staving off a receivership. This would benefit policyholders by helping to stabilize the

This bill offers a reasonable and balanced framework to ensure the stability of both the Federal Home Loan Bank system, and the broader financial system by addressing key concerns when an insurer faces receivership. Federal Home Loan Banks play a vital role in supporting insurers by providing liquidity to ensure that they can meet their financial obligations. However, when an insurer enters receivership, this balance is disrupted, and swift, clear actions are needed to prevent further destabilization of the market. This bill would lessen the above-mentioned risk.

Testimony of Peter M. Gore with Maine Street Solutions
On behalf of Maine Employers Mutual Insurance Company
in support of LD 720, An Act to Protect Federal Home Loan Banks That Lend

March 11, 2025
Senator Bailey, Representative Matheson, Members of the HCIFS Committee, I am Peter Gore, with Maine Street Solutions, providing you with the comments and support of my client, Maine Employers Mutual Insurance Company, otherwise known as MEMIC, in support of LD 720, An Act to Protect Federal Home Loan Banks That Lend Money to Insurer Members That Become Delinquent.
MEMIC is Maine's largest workers' compensation insurer. MEMIC was created out of the legislatively approved comp reforms of 1992. We are a mutually owned company, with over 17,000 policy holders employing nearly 200,000 employees. We currently provide workers' comp coverage for over 60% of the commercially insured market. By emphasizing safety, reducing injuries, operating our company efficiently and having a stable system, we have been able to return money to our Maine policyholders - mainly our small businesses - for the last 25 years. The average check has been about $1,300.
MEMIC is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston. The FHLBank is a valuable resource for members that seek to efficiently manage their balance sheets and build capital that protects their policyholders. LD 720 extends certain protections to a Federal Home Loan Bank for any pledge, security, credit, collateral, loan, advance, reimbursement or guarantee agreement or arrangement or any similar agreement or arrangement or other credit enhancement to which such bank is a party with an insurance company that is under conservation, rehabilitation, liquidated on or administrative supervision by the Maine Bureau of Insurance.
Were LD 720 to pass, MEMIC's ability to access the FHLBank facility would increase about $61 million. This significantly increases our ability to manage our balance sheet, to the benefit of our insureds. And since we are licensed in 46 states and the District of Columbia, not having this law available in Maine has created a financial disadvantage for us compared to our competitors in the 30 states that have adopted this legislation. While this is technical bill in appearance, it is simply a rational, safe, and economically advantageous amendment to our laws that creates a fair playing field for all members of Federal Home Loan Banks, and most importantly, protects and benefits policyholders of insurers that might slip into receivership.

We would also point out that this legislation includes provisions recommended by the NAIC and require the FHLBank to work closely with the Bureau in the very unlikely event of a Maine insurer entering receivership. LD 720 also reflects a model act adopted by the National Council of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL), so that you can be assured by these two facts that the legislation is a positive step for Maine.
We strongly urge you to support this legislation. I can be present at the work session should you have questions. Thank you for the opportunity for us to provide you with our comments.
